EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions remain critically high across the Middle East with significant developments in the US-Iran diplomatic efforts, ongoing cross-border escalations between Israel and Lebanon, and direct military engagements in the Persian Gulf. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu announced IDF forces have crossed the Litani River into southern Lebanon, marking a significant escalation, while Iran's air defenses successfully shot down a US-Israeli drone near Qeshm Island, coinciding with intense diplomatic rhetoric between Washington and Tehran regarding a potential nuclear deal and Strait of Hormuz status.

IRAN
Iran's air defenses shot down a US-Israeli Orbiter drone near Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf early on 30 May, with wreckage found on Qeshm. This occurred amidst ongoing US-Iran negotiations, with US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth stating talks are progressing but also warning of renewed US attacks if no deal is reached. US President Trump outlined specific demands for a deal, including Iran never acquiring nuclear weapons, immediate opening of the Strait of Hormuz without fees, and destruction of enriched uranium. Iran's Foreign Ministry and IRGC-affiliated sources, however, reject Trump's claims as a "distortion of reality" and "mixture of truth and lies," denying any agreement on dismantling nuclear materials or opening Hormuz without Iranian terms, which include an immediate payment of $12 billion in frozen assets and a full ceasefire in Lebanon. Internally, a political struggle continues, with hardliners pushing against a deal, while President Pezeshkian and Speaker Qalibaf previously warned the Supreme Leader of severe economic crisis and potential mass protests if no agreement is reached. The IRGC Navy claims 20 ships transited Hormuz in the last 24 hours under their coordination. Press TV reports that Iran's counterterrorism forces eliminated two terrorists in Kermanshah. Power stations of some industries were damaged in recent "war," according to the Deputy Minister of Energy.

ISRAEL
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed that IDF's 36th Division forces have crossed the Litani River and advanced toward strategic points in southern Lebanon, also stating operations are occurring in Beirut and Beqaa. The northern Israeli front faced significant drone and rocket attacks from Lebanon. Hezbollah drones struck a military zone near Shomera in the Western Galilee, and another drone was intercepted. Over 15 rockets were fired overnight towards northern Israel, with one directly hitting a commercial center in Kiryat Shmona, causing extensive damage but no reported casualties. Several other rockets were intercepted. The IDF responded by destroying Hezbollah rocket launchers in southern Lebanon and conducting airstrikes and artillery attacks in southern Lebanon. In Gaza, IDF forces eliminated four armed Hamas operatives yesterday, with three struck near troops in the south and one sniper in the north. A 22-year-old was lightly injured by stone-throwing on Route 60 near Sela in Samaria. The Chief of Staff, Major General Eyal Zamir, visited the Druze community for Eid al-Adha, emphasizing the deep bond between the IDF and the Druze community.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Four Hamas gunmen who "posed an immediate threat to troops" were killed in Israeli strikes in the Gaza Strip yesterday. Three armed Hamas operatives were struck near troops in the south, and one Hamas operative planning a sniper attack was struck and killed in the Strip's north. The UN has reiterated that 100% of Gaza belongs to Palestinians, denouncing Israeli PM Netanyahu's plans to expand control over Gaza as illegal. Dr. Jamal Abu Aoun, a healthcare worker, was killed in an Israeli strike on Deir Al-Balah.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched multiple attacks against northern Israel, including drone intrusions into the Western Galilee near Shomera and Kfar Giladi/Metulla, and a barrage of over 15 rockets targeting Kiryat Shmona and other northern communities overnight. One rocket caused direct damage to a commercial center in Kiryat Shmona. Hezbollah also targeted an Israeli Merkava tank in Zawtar al-Sharqiya with a drone and multiple Merkava tanks in Yahr and Tebnin with guided missiles. The IDF confirmed destroying Hezbollah rocket launchers in southern Lebanon that were used in overnight attacks and published footage showing Hezbollah rockets striking Saint Georges Orthodox Church and other buildings in Marjaayoun. Israeli forces issued an evacuation warning for the villages of Mifdon, Zabdin, and Shukin in southern Lebanon. US-hosted trilateral military talks involving Lebanon, Israel, and the US concluded without a ceasefire agreement, with Israel insisting on continued operations and a buffer zone, and Lebanon emphasizing the need for a ceasefire and Israeli withdrawal.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Fighter jets were observed flying over Baghdad, Iraq. The process of integrating Muqtada al-Sadr's Saraya al-Salam military wing into the Iraqi armed forces has begun. The Iraqi Prime Minister stated the government is determined to advance the project of exclusively holding weapons in state hands. An Iraqi official reports that approximately 20,000 ISIS members escaped Syrian prisons due to security gaps and fled to the Iraqi borders. A special force arrested Adnan Mohammed Hammoud Al-Jamili, Iraqi Deputy Oil Minister and Director General of Baiji Refineries, on corruption charges. The Marashda-Al-Baghouz bridge in eastern Deir Ezzor, near the Iraqi-Syrian border, collapsed due to the Euphrates River flood. The US Special Envoy to Syria and Iraq, Tom Brack, will continue his central role after his term as special envoy to Syria ended. An Iraqi security delegation, led by Qassem al-Araji, is set to visit Tehran to implement a security memorandum of understanding between Iran and Iraq.

GULF STATES
Oman's Maritime Security Center urged vessels to exercise caution due to a floating object suspected to be a naval mine west of the inshore traffic zone in the Strait of Hormuz. The US Navy also issued a provocative statement warning mariners and aviators of dangerous military operations in Hormuz to counter alleged Iranian mining activities, advising them to coordinate with the US Navy. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that the UAE conducted dozens of airstrikes against Iran throughout the war, in coordination with the US and Israel, targeting sites like South Pars gas field, Asaluyeh energy complex, Qeshm, Abu Musa islands, Bandar Abbas, and Lavan Island oil refinery. Saudi Arabia reportedly complained to the US that UAE attacks on Iran were raising the risk of regional energy facilities coming under Iranian fire and wanted the US to pressure the UAE to stop. Qatar’s Deputy PM stated that while Doha opposes permanent fees for Hormuz passage, temporary fees are negotiable to restore normal traffic. Qatar also reportedly agreed to provide Iran with $6 billion in credit for food and medical supplies instead of direct cash, contingent on Iranian compliance with conditions like opening Hormuz and mine clearance.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **IDF Crosses Litani River:** Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed that IDF's 36th Division forces have crossed the Litani River into southern Lebanon and advanced to strategic points.
2.  **Iran Downs US-Israeli Drone:** Iran's air defense forces shot down a US-Israeli Orbiter drone near Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf.
3.  **Hezbollah Rocket Strike on Kiryat Shmona:** Over 15 rockets from Lebanon hit northern Israel, with one causing significant direct damage to a commercial center in Kiryat Shmona.
4.  **US-Iran Nuclear Talks & Hormuz:** US President Trump announced specific demands for a deal with Iran, including no nuclear weapons and free passage through Hormuz, while Iran denies any final agreement and rejects key US conditions.
5.  **US Personnel Injured in Kuwait:** Five American military personnel and contractors were injured, and two US MQ-9 Reaper drones were seriously damaged at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait due to debris from an intercepted Iranian ballistic missile attack on 27 May.
6.  **UAE Airstrikes on Iran:** The Wall Street Journal reported that the UAE carried out dozens of airstrikes against Iran, in coordination with the US and Israel, targeting energy infrastructure and islands in the Strait of Hormuz.
7.  **Oman Mine Alert:** Oman's Maritime Security Center warned vessels about a floating object suspected to be a naval mine in its territorial waters in the Strait of Hormuz.
8.  **Iraqi Militia Integration:** The process of integrating Muqtada al-Sadr's Saraya al-Salam into the Iraqi armed forces has begun, with the Iraqi PM emphasizing exclusive state control of weapons.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks in the Lebanon-Israel theater are critically high following Netanyahu's announcement of IDF ground operations beyond the Litani River and continued intense cross-border attacks. The downing of a US-Israeli drone near Qeshm Island by Iran raises concerns about direct engagement in the Persian Gulf, especially given the US warnings of "dangerous military operations" in Hormuz. The ongoing, complex US-Iran negotiations, characterized by conflicting public statements and deep disagreements on nuclear and Hormuz issues, suggest high instability and potential for miscalculation, with a renewed US military option against Iran explicitly stated. The alleged UAE airstrikes against Iranian energy targets, and Saudi complaints about their destabilizing effect, indicate a broadening regional conflict.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** Secretary of War Pete Hegseth stated that the US is in a "good place" for a deal with Iran but is ready to renew attacks if an agreement isn't reached. President Trump publicly detailed conditions for a deal, including Iran never having nuclear weapons, immediate free passage through Hormuz, and destruction of enriched uranium, while also claiming a naval blockade on Iran would be lifted. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the seizure of approximately $1 billion in Iranian crypto assets and the tracking of Iranian officials' European properties.
**Qatar:** Qatar reportedly agreed to provide Iran with $6 billion in credit for humanitarian goods, not cash, contingent on specific Iranian actions, and stated that temporary transit fees for Hormuz are negotiable.
**European Union:** A survey suggests a majority of EU citizens favor a foreign policy shift away from the US. The EU announced new sanctions against Hamas and Islamic Jihad.
**Oman:** Oman assured the US it has no plans to implement transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz after US warnings of sanctions.
**Pakistan:** Pakistan reaffirmed its commitment to an independent Palestinian state, stating no change in its stance towards Israel without it.
**China:** China denied US allegations of supplying man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS) to Iran, which allegedly downed a US F-15E jet, and a long-range radar.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the status and terms of a potential US-Iran agreement. US President Trump declared specific demands for a deal and claimed a naval blockade was being lifted, but Iranian officials vehemently deny a final agreement, labeling Trump's remarks as "distortion of reality" and "a mixture of truth and lies." Iran also emphasizes that no money will be transferred without prior conditions met, contradicting Trump's "no money until further notice" statement. Unverified claims of "tens of thousands" celebrating Supreme Leader Khamenei's assassination in Tehran circulated, which appear to be sensationalized or outright propaganda given the lack of credible corroboration. The US military has not confirmed Iran's placement of mines in the Strait of Hormuz despite Trump's assertions and ongoing searches. Reports regarding alleged UAE airstrikes on Iranian territory (Wall Street Journal) are significant but require further independent verification regarding scale and frequency. The incident involving US troops injured in Kuwait from Iranian missile debris on 27 May, as reported by Bloomberg and Press TV, was only officially confirmed by CENTCOM as an interception. The claim of a Chinese-made MANPADS downing a US F-15E in Iran (NBC) is unconfirmed by official US sources.
